THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT PRAYING TO MODIFY THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 27.01.2015 PASSED IN MVC NO.1596/2012 ON THE FILE OF THE MEMBER, PRINCIPAL MACT, BANGALORE,
PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
THESE MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEALS COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, K.S.MUDAGAL J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:

JUDGMENT Challenging the award in MVC No.1596/2012 on the file of Principal MACT, (SCCH-01) the Insurer has preferred MFA No.3979/2015 and claimants have preferred MFA No.2278/2015.
2.
The appellants in MFA No.2278/2015 were the claimants and respondents in the said case were respondents Nos.1 and 2 before the Tribunal.
For the purpose of NC: 2023:KHC:21221-DB convenience, the parties will be referred to henceforth according to their ranks before the Tribunal.
3. Claimant Nos.1 and 2 are the father and mother of deceased Manjunath.

On 19.02.2012 at 1 a.m.
when Manjunath was riding his motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-01/EU-9931 at Doddanekkundi signal near Bhagini Hotel within the limits of K.R Puram Traffic Police Station, the lorry bearing registration No.TN-02/T-9592 hit him and caused the accident.
Due to the injuries suffered in the accident, Manjunath died at the spot.

Regarding the accident, one Nethravathi filed complaint before K.R. Puram traffic police station, alleging that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry bearing registration No.TN-02/T-9592.
4.

On the basis of the said complaint, K.R. Puram Traffic police registered FIR as per Ex.P1 in Crime No.30/2012 against the driver of the lorry for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 304A of IPC.
At the relevant time, respondent Nos.1 and 2 were the insurer and registered owner of the said lorry.

The claimants filed MVC No.1596/2012 before the Tribunal claiming compensation of NC: 2023:KHC:21221-DB Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents on the ground that accident and consequent death of Manjunath occurred solely due to the negligence of the driver of the lorry.
They further contended that they were solely depending on the income of the deceased and due to his death, they have suffered the damages.

sentences.text: Respondent No.2 did not contest the petition.
Respondent No.1 alone contested the petition denying the occurrence of the accident due to actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry.
Respondent No.1 contended that the deceased himself was solely responsible for the accident.
Respondent No.1 disputed the age, occupation, income of the deceased and its liability to pay the compensation.

It was alleged that the lorry was operating in violation of the permit condition,
thereby there was breach of policy condition and it was not liable to pay the compensation.
6. To substantiate their claim, claimants got examined PWs.1 to 4 and got marked Exs.P1 to P.20.

Respondent No.1 examined its official as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R.1 to R4.
NC: 2023:KHC:21221-DB 7.

The Tribunal on hearing the parties relying on Ex.P1 to P7 and the oral evidence held that the accident occurred due to the contributory negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry as well as the deceased.
The Tribunal apportioned the negligence as 75% and 25% between the driver of the lorry and deceased Manjunath.

Further the Tribunal relying on the evidence of PW.4 and Exs.P8, 9,
17 to 20 held that the deceased was working as Territory Business Manager with Astra Zeneca Pharma India Ltd.
The Tribunal further held that since he had variable income, taking the average of 8 months income considered his income at Rs.31,000/- per month.
After deducting 10% for income tax, considered his annual income at Rs.3,59,800/-.

8. The Tribunal considered the age of the deceased at 26 years, added 50% of his income by way of future prospects, deducted 50% of his income for his personal expenses, applied 17 multiplier and awarded compensation of Rs.63,24,000/- on the head of loss of dependency.

The Tribunal in all awarded the compensation of Rs.48,25,500/- on different heads as per the table below:

4 challenged the award on the ground of negligence as well as quantum of compensation.

sentences.text: Sri Janardhan Reddy, learned Counsel appearing for the insurer reiterating the grounds of the appeal submits that claimants' own documents show that the deceased was solely responsible for the accident.
He further submits that future prospects considered by the Tribunal is on the higher side.
He further submits that there was breach of policy condition as the vehicle had operated in violation of the permit.
Therefore, the Tribunal should have exonerated the insurer of its liability.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the claimants submits that the Tribunal erred in holding that the deceased contributed 25% negligence for the accident.
He further submits that the assessment of the income of the deceased by the Tribunal was erroneous.
The Tribunal should have taken the income as per the salary slips produced by the claimants.
Thus he seeks enhancement of the compensation.

So far as the liability of the Insurer he submits that the charge sheet was not filed regarding the violation of any terms of the policy condition under Motor Vehicles Act and such violation of permit was not proved.
Therefore, the Insurer is liable to pay the compensation.

12. On hearing both side and on perusal of the records, the points that arise for consideration are:
(i) Whether the finding of the Tribunal that the accident occurred due to contributory negligence of the driver of the lorry and the deceased at the rate of 75% and 25%
suffers any illegality?
(ii) Whether the compensation awarded is just and fair one?
(iii) Whether insurer is liable to pay the compensation?"
NC: 2023:KHC:21221-DB Reg. Negligence:
13. Both side do not dispute the occurrence of the accident.
PW.1/first claimant was not the eyewitness to the incident.
PWs.2 and 3 though were examined as eyewitnesses, as rightly observed by the Tribunal, they were not the complainants.
PW.4 was not even the charge sheet witness.
However, on investigation the charge sheet Ex.P7 was filed against the driver of the lorry.

14. The coordinate Bench of this Court in Veerappa and another vs. Siddappa and another1 has held that the charge sheet is not the conclusive proof of the negligence in the proceedings under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act and the Court has to examine the same with reference to the other evidence adduced by the parties.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case Ex.P2 the sketch of scene of accident produced by the claimants themselves shows that the accident took place at junction.
It further shows that the lorry was crossing the road at the junction and the deceased was coming on the main road.

When the lorry driver had almost crossed the junction and reached the border of the road, the accident has United India Insurance Co. Ltd vs Sri Adinarayana Reddy on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54013007/

sentences.text: Considering the same, the Tribunal has rightly held that both the deceased and the driver of the lorry have contributed to the occurrence of the accident.
The Tribunal held since the lorry was crossing the road, the driver of the lorry should have been more vigilant and watchful.
The Tribunal rightly apportioned the contributory negligence to him at 75%.
The said finding does not suffer any illegality.

Reg. Quantum:
15.
Ex. P10
the SSLC marks card of the deceased shows his date of birth as 13.06.1986.
The accident took place on 19.02.2012.
The Tribunal rightly considered his age as 26 years as on the date of the accident.
The claimants to substantiate their contention that the deceased was working with Astra Zeneca Pharma India Ltd as Territory Manager examined PW.4 and produced his salary slips Exs.P9 and P20.

They also produced Ex.P8 the appointment confirmation letter, Ex.P11 pan card,
Ex.P17 the appointment letter, Ex.P18 the service confirmation letter and Ex.P19 the application for the employment relating to the victim.

16. Those documents coupled with the evidence of PW.4 the Manager of Astra Zeneca Pharma India Ltd., showed that deceased was working as Territory Business Manager in - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:21221-DB Astra Zeneca Pharma India Ltd. since 07.04.2011 till the said accident and drawing salary at Rs.32,436/- and his last drawn salary was Rs.32,436/-.
The salary slips attached include incentives.
Therefore, the Tribunal rightly took the average of eight months salary as consistent salary at Rs.31,000/-p.m.
The Tribunal added 50% to the said income by way of future prospects.
The records show that the deceased was employed in a Private Sector Organization.
There was nothing to show that; that was permanent employment.
Therefore, in view of judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi2, the Tribunal should have taken the future prospects at 40%.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 17. Since the deceased was bachelor, 50% of his income has to be deducted for his personal expenses.
Therefore, annual income of the deceased would be Rs.3,72,000/- (Rs.31,000/- x 12).
However, 10% of the taxable income has to be deducted towards payment of taxes.
Such deduction comes to Rs.12,200/-.
Therefore his annual income comes to Rs.3,59,800/-.

On deducting 50% for his personal expenses, his annual income becomes Rs.1,79,900/- 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC)
- 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:21221-DB 40% of the same comes to Rs.71,960/-.
Therefore, his annual income comes to Rs.1,79,900/- + Rs.71,960/- = Rs.2,51,860/-.
The applicable multiplier to the age of the deceased is '17'.
Therefore, the damages on the head of loss of dependency comes to Rs.2,51,860/- x 17= 42,81,620/-.

sentences.text: As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi's case referred to supra, each of the claimants are entitled for compensation under the head of Consortium at Rs.40,000/- with escalation at 10% for every three years.
Similarly for conventional heads i.e. Funeral Expenses and Loss of Estate, they are entitled for a compensation of Rs.15,000/- + 15,000/- with escalation at 10% for every three years.

Therefore, the total damages on account of death of deceased is as follows:
 Sl. Heads Compensation  No. amount in Rs.
 1. Loss of dependency 42,81,620/-
 2. Loss of Consortium 96,000/-
 3. Loss of conventional Heads 36,000/-

Total 44,13,620/-
After deducting 25% towards negligence on the part of the deceased himself
The Insurer contended that the vehicle was operated in Bengaluru in Karnataka State whereas the permit was issued only to operate in Tamil Nadu.
To substantiate the said contention, the Insurer relied on the evidence of RW.1 and Ex.R2.

In Ex.R2, the condition with regard to route permit is as follows:
"All routes except those prohibited"
20.
The Insurer did not examine Regional Transport Authority who issued Ex.R2 to show that the Karnataka route was prohibited route.
There was nothing to show that Bengaluru where the accident took place was prohibited route.

Considering non-examination of material witnesses, the Tribunal rightly held that contention of the Insurer with regard to breach of permit condition is not proved and fastened the liability to the Insurer.
That finding does not warrant any interference.
21. In the light of the above discussion, both the appeals deserve to be allowed in part.

Hence, the following:
- 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:21221-DB ORDER
The appeals are partly allowed.
The impugned award of the Tribunal is modified as follows:
(i) The claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.33,10,215/- with interest thereon at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation.
